html:
The 2010 Osh clashes were days of killing between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks in the cities of Osh and Jalal-Abad, in southern Kyrgyzstan, in June 2010.

Tension had grown in the weeks after the April revolution, in a region where the Soviet border drawn in the 1920s had left a large Uzbek minority. Fighting broke out in Osh on the night of 10 June. Armed mobs, some helped by soldiers, burned whole Uzbek districts. Official counts gave over 400 dead, most of them Uzbeks, and hundreds of thousands fled, many briefly into Uzbekistan.

An international inquiry found that some attacks on Uzbek districts could amount to crimes against humanity. Most of those jailed afterwards were Uzbeks. The clashes deepened mistrust in the Fergana valley, where Osh is the main city.
sum: The 2010 Osh clashes were days of killing between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks in the cities of Osh and Jalal-Abad, in southern Kyrgyzstan, in June 2010.
